Accessing the OpenShift web console

  • The OpenShift web console provides access to all the cluster functionality, including pod creation and application deployment.

    To access OpenShift through a web browser:

    1. Get the console URL of the routes.
    1. Get the existing routes in all namespaces by running the following command:

    [core@csah-pri ~]$ oc get routes --all-namespaces | grep -i console-openshift

    openshift-console          console             console-openshift-console.apps.ocp.dcws.lab                       console             https   reencrypt/Redirect     None

    The URL in the openshift-console namespace is console-openshift-console.apps.ocp.dcws.lab.

    1. Paste the URL into a web browser and log in using the kubeadmin credentials.

Agent-based installer cluster deployment

  • Introduction

    The agent-based installer can run offline and is useful for clusters that are in a restricted network without Internet access.

    Note: A mirror registry is required for disconnected installations. Various options are available for the mirror registry, including Red Hat Quay, JFrog Artifactory, and Harbor. For more information, see About disconnected installation mirroring. The container images must be mirrored before you start the deployment.

    The Mirror Registry for Red Hat OpenShift is only designed for initial cluster deployment when no other registry is available for use. Dell Technologies recommends a highly available setup for the OpenShift mirror registry, such as Red Hat Quay. The following section of this guide describes the process for mirroring only the OpenShift Container Platform image repository that is needed for the initial cluster deployment and not designed to be the ongoing registry in a production environment. For information about mirroring the custom catalogs that are required for operator installation, see Mirroring images for a disconnected installation.

    Prerequisites

    Ensure that:

    • A node is installed that has Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 or 9 with Podman 3.4.2 or later and OpenSSL.
    • A DNS-configured A record is available for the server to access the registry service using FQDN. For more information, see DNS A record.

    Install a mirror registry

    To install a mirror registry for Red Hat OpenShift:

    1. From the OpenShift console Downloads page, download the mirror-registry.tar.gz package for the latest Red Hat OpenShift mirror registry version (Red Hat access credentials are required).
    1. To copy the package to the mirror registry server and unpack the package, run the following tar command:

    tar -xvf mirror-registry.tar.gz

    1. Install the mirror registry for Red Hat OpenShift on your mirror registry host by running the following command:

    ./mirror-registry install --quayHostname <fqdn of the mirror registry host> --quayRoot <installation directory>

    Use an absolute path for quayRoot when running the mirror registry script.

    Note: Make a note of the init user credentials in the output of the preceding command. These credentials are required for access to the mirror registry CLI and user interface (UI).

    1. To log in to the registry using the username and password that you generated, run the following command:

    podman login -u init -p <password> https://<fqdn of the mirror registry host>:8443

    Note: If there is a certificate issue, copy the rootCA.pem that is in the <installation directory>/quay-rootCA  folder to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and run the update-ca-trust command to update the certificates.

    1. To access the UI, paste the following URL into a browser:

    https://<fqdn of the mirror registry host>:8443

    1. Copy the pullsecret from the Red Hat OpenShift web console and create the JSON file by running the following command:

    cat ./pull-secret | jq . > <path>/<pull_secret_file_in_json>

    1. To generate a base64-encoded username and password or token for the mirror registry, run the following command:

    echo -n '<user_name>:<password>' | base64 -w0

    1. To edit the JSON file, run <path>/<pull_secret_file_in_json> and add the section for your registry credentials.

      "auths": {

        "<mirror_registry>": {

          "auth": "<credentials in base64 format generated in previous step>",

          "email": "<email id>"

        }

      }

    Mirror the OpenShift image repository

    Ensure that the mirror registry host has Internet access, an then perform the following steps:

    1. Determine the version of OpenShift Container Platform that you want to install and the corresponding tag from the Repository Tags page.
    1. To set the required environment variables, run the following command:

    #Export the release version, change the version as required:

    OCP_RELEASE=4.14.0

    #Export the local registry name and host port:

    LOCAL_REGISTRY='<fqdn of the mirror registry host>:8443'

    #Export the local repository name:

    LOCAL_REPOSITORY='ocp4/openshift414'

    #Export the name of the repository to mirror:

    PRODUCT_REPO='openshift-release-dev'

    #Export the path to your registry pull secret:

    LOCAL_SECRET_JSON='<path to pullsecret file in json format>'

    #Export the release mirror:

    RELEASE_NAME="ocp-release"

    #Export the type of architecture for your server:

    ARCHITECTURE=x86_64

    1. To push the release images to the local registry, run the following command:

    oc adm release mirror -a ${LOCAL_SECRET_JSON} --from=quay.io/${PRODUCT_REPO}/${RELEASE_NAME}:${OCP_RELEASE}-${ARCHITECTURE} --to=${LOCAL_REGISTRY}/${LOCAL_REPOSITORY} --to-release-image=${LOCAL_REGISTRY}/${LOCAL_REPOSITORY}:${OCP_RELEASE}-${ARCHITECTURE}

    This command pulls the release information as a digest. The information about mirrors is unique to the mirrored repository.

    The command output includes the imageContentSources data that is required during the cluster installation. Note down the imageContentSources data to add to the install-config.yaml file during the cluster installation. The following code excerpt is from the imageContentSources section:

    imageContentSources:

    - mirrors:

      - csah.dcws.lab:8443/ocp4/openshift414

      source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release

    - mirrors:

      - csah.dcws.lab:8443/ocp4/openshift414

      source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev

    1. Log in to the UI using init user and verify that the version images that you want are pushed to the mirror registry.

    Figure 7.        Mirror registry for OpenShift

    Run the agent-based installer

    The CSAH node is used for running the installer.

    To start the deployment:

    1. Log in to the Red Hat OpenShift web console using your Red Hat credentials.
    1. On the Datacenter tab, click Run Agent-based Installer locally.
    2. On the Install OpenShift on Bare Metal locally with Agent page, select Linux as the operating system for the OpenShift Installer.
    3. Copy the Download Installer link. Edit the URL from “stable” to the version of the installation program that you want by running the following command:

    https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/clients/ocp/stable/openshift-install-linux.tar.gz

    The images version that is already downloaded in the mirror registry must match that version. For example, if you want to deploy a cluster on version 4.14.0, ensure that you have downloaded the 4.14.0 images into the mirror registry.

    1. To download the installer and extract it onto the CSAH node, run the following command:

    wget https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/clients/ocp/4.14.0/openshift-install-linux.tar.gz

    tar -xzvf openshift-install-linux.tar.gz

    cp openshift-install /usr/local/bin

    1. To install the nmstate package, run the following command:

    sudo dnf install /usr/bin/nmstatectl -y

    1. Create a directory to store the install configuration by running the following command:

    mkdir ~/dir-install

    1. Use this sample yaml file to create install-config.yaml in the install directory that you created in the previous step, updating fields if required.
    2. Use this sample yaml file file to create agent-config.yaml in the install directory that you created in the previous step, updating fields if required.

    Note: Ensure that the file names are install-config.yaml and agent-config.yaml and that the files are present in the installation directory.

    1. Convert the pull secret file that you created in JSON format to text format by running the following command:

    tr -d '[:space:]' < <pull scret file in json format>

    1. Copy the edited pullsecret.txt file content to the install-config.yaml file.
    2. Create the agent image by running the following command:

    openshift-install --dir dir-install/ agent create image

    1. Boot the cluster nodes with the agent.x86_64.iso image.
    2. Run the following command to know when the bootstrap host (the rendezvous host) reboots:

    openshift-install --dir dir-install/ agent wait-for bootstrap-complete --log-level=debug

    Figure 8.        Bootstrap status command output (example)

    1. Track the progress of the installation and verify that it is successful by running the following command:

    openshift-install --dir dir-install agent wait-for install-complete

    The following figure shows the command output from a successful installation:

    Figure 9.        Installation status (sample output)

    1. Use the kubeconfig and kubeadmin credentials from the command output to access the cluster.

    The command output includes the imageContentSources data that is required during the cluster installation. Note down the imageContentSources data to add to the install-config.yaml file during the cluster installation. The following code excerpt is from the imageContentSources section:

    imageContentSources:

    - mirrors:

      - csah.dcws.lab:8443/ocp4/openshift414

      source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release

    - mirrors:

      - csah.dcws.lab:8443/ocp4/openshift414

      source: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-v4.0-art-dev

    1. Log in to the UI using init user and verify that the version images that you want are pushed to the mirror registry.

    Figure 7.        Mirror registry for OpenShift

Agent-based installer cluster deployment

  • Run the agent-based installer

    The CSAH node is used for running the installer.

    To start the deployment:

    1. Log in to the Red Hat OpenShift web console using your Red Hat credentials.
    1. On the Datacenter tab, click Run Agent-based Installer locally.
    2. On the Install OpenShift on Bare Metal locally with Agent page, select Linux as the operating system for the OpenShift Installer.
    3. Copy the Download Installer link. Edit the URL from “stable” to the version of the installation program that you want by running the following command:

    https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/clients/ocp/stable/openshift-install-linux.tar.gz

    The images version that is already downloaded in the mirror registry must match that version. For example, if you want to deploy a cluster on version 4.14.0, ensure that you have downloaded the 4.14.0 images into the mirror registry.

    1. To download the installer and extract it onto the CSAH node, run the following command:

    wget https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/clients/ocp/4.14.0/openshift-install-linux.tar.gz

    tar -xzvf openshift-install-linux.tar.gz

    cp openshift-install /usr/local/bin

    1. To install the nmstate package, run the following command:

    sudo dnf install /usr/bin/nmstatectl -y

    1. Create a directory to store the install configuration by running the following command:

    mkdir ~/dir-install

    1. Use this sample yaml file to create install-config.yaml in the install directory that you created in the previous step, updating fields if required.
    2. Use this sample yaml file file to create agent-config.yaml in the install directory that you created in the previous step, updating fields if required.

    Note: Ensure that the file names are install-config.yaml and agent-config.yaml and that the files are present in the installation directory.

    1. Convert the pull secret file that you created in JSON format to text format by running the following command:

    tr -d '[:space:]' < <pull scret file in json format>

    1. Copy the edited pullsecret.txt file content to the install-config.yaml file.
    2. Create the agent image by running the following command:

    openshift-install --dir dir-install/ agent create image

    1. Boot the cluster nodes with the agent.x86_64.iso image.
    2. Run the following command to know when the bootstrap host (the rendezvous host) reboots:

    openshift-install --dir dir-install/ agent wait-for bootstrap-complete --log-level=debug

    Figure 8.        Bootstrap status command output (example)

    1. Track the progress of the installation and verify that it is successful by running the following command:

    openshift-install --dir dir-install agent wait-for install-complete

    The following figure shows the command output from a successful installation:

    Figure 9.        Installation status (sample output)

    1. Use the kubeconfig and kubeadmin credentials from the command output to access the cluster.

Assisted Installer deployment

  • Use the Assisted Installer that is available on the Red Hat hybrid cloud console (access requires Red Hat login credentials).

    Prerequisites

    Ensure that:

    • The oc-client is installed on the CSAH node. The client is available on the Red Hat OpenShift downloads page (access requires Red Hat login credentials).
    • DNS is present in the network, with entries for the cluster nodes. Add the following entries to the DNS:
    • api.<cluster-name>.<base-domain> API VIP
    • *.apps.<cluster-name>.<base-domain> Ingress VIP

    Note: Ensure that there is no wildcard entry such as *.<cluster-name>.<base-domain> on the DNS.

    Configure DNS on the CSAH node

    To configure DNS on the CSAH node (if it is not already present in the network):

    1. Download the Ansible playbooks from GitHub and check out branch ecws_ocp414 by running the following command:

    [ansible@csah-ai ~]$ git clone https://github.com/dell-esg/openshift-bare-metal.git

    [ansible@csah-ai ~]$ cd <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal

    [ansible@csah-ai openshift-bare-metal]$ git checkout origin/ecws_ocp414

    1. Prepare and run the Ansible playbooks as user ansible.
    2. Update the YAML file containing information about the control-plane, and compute nodes.

    Note: Ensure that you modify only values in the file. Keys must always remain the same.

    1. Run the program by running the following command:

    cd <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/python

    [ansible@csah-ai python]$ python3 generate_inventory_file.py

    –-run --id_user <idrac user> --id_pass <idrac password> –-nodes nodes.yaml

    Note: If the iDRAC user and password are the same across all control-plane and compute nodes, run the program using the --id_user and --id_pass arguments.

    1. When the following prompt appears, enter yes or No based on whether there is a backup management node:

    Is there a backup management node [yes/No]: No

    1. Select Assisted Installer as the install type, and enter 3.

    installation type:

     1. UPI

     2. IPI

     3. Assisted Installer

    enter install type: 3

    The next option lets you set up a DNS server on the CSAH node or use an existing DNS in the network.

    1. Select the DNS options that you require. The following code excerpt deploys the DNS on the CSAH node:

    Do you want to install DNS on CSAH [yes/No]: yes

    specify a DNS forwarder if necessary (yes/No): yes

    enter the DNS forwarder IP: 10.8.8.8

    specify cluster name

    default [ocp]: ai-414

    specify zone file

    default [/var/named/ai-414.zones]:

    enter API virtual IP: 192.168.36.31
    adding api_ip: 192.168.36.61

    enter ingress virtual IP: 192.168.36.62
    adding wildcard_ip: 192.168.36.62

    1. If DHCP is required on the CSAH node, enter yes at the following prompt and provide the requested details:

    Do you want to install DHCP server on CSAH [yes/No]:

    1. Review and generate the inventory file.

    The program creates two files in the <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/python directory: generated_inventory and ansible.yaml.

    1. Copy both files into the <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/ansible directory.
    2. As user ansible, run the playbooks:

    [ansible@csah-ai ansible] $ pwd

    /home/ansible/openshift-bare-metal/ansible

    [ansible@csah-ai ansible] $ ansible-playbook -i generated_inventory ansible.yaml

    Create a cluster

    To create a cluster using the Assisted Installer UI:

    1. Log in to Red Hat Assisted Installer using your Red Hat credentials.
    2. Select the Clusters tab and click Create cluster.
    3. Select the Datacenter tab and click Create cluster.
    4. Click Create Cluster again and provide the following information in the wizard:
    • Cluster name 
    • Base domain

    Note: All DNS records must be subdomains of this base domain and include the cluster name. You cannot change the base domain after installing the cluster.

    • OpenShift Container Platform version

    Figure 2.        Creating a cluster using Assisted Installer

    1. For a single node deployment, select Install single node OpenShift (SNO) and click Next.
    2. Under Hosts’ network configuration, select DHCP only or Static IP, bridges, and bonds as required.

    If you select Static IP, bridges, and bonds the Static network configurations tab is enabled.

    1. Select one of the following options:
    • Form view for basic network configuration, where advanced features such as bonds, bridges, and so on are not required.
    • YAML view to configure the network using nmstate config, allowing advanced network configurations for the cluster nodes.

    To use nmstate config in the YAML view, see this sample file.

    Enter the required information and click Next.

    1. On the Operators page, select any required operators and click Next.
    2. On the Host discovery page, click Add host.
    3. Add the SSH public key of the CSAH node to the Public key field and select Full image file to boot with a USB drive or PXE.

    Note: You can use an existing SSH key on the CSAH node or generate a new key pair using ssh-keygen. Enter the required details as prompted.

    1. Click Generate Discovery ISO.

    Figure 3.        Generating the discovery ISO

    1. Download the discovery ISO and boot the server using virtual media.

    After 15 minutes, the host is discovered and displayed on the Assisted Installer portal, as shown in the following figure:

    Figure 4.        Host discovery on the Assisted Installer portal

    1. If required, change the hostname of the nodes.

    Select the Role of the nodes, master or worker, and click Next.

    1. On the Storage page, select the Installation disk for each node as required and click Next.
    2. On the Networking page, select a subnet from the available subnets. Then:
      1. Enter API and Ingress virtual IP addresses.

    Note: An API virtual IP address provides an endpoint for all users to interact with and configure the platform. An Ingress virtual IP address provides an endpoint for application traffic flowing from outside the cluster. Ensure that the DNS is configured with entries for API and Ingress IP addresses.

    1. Ensure that Use the same host discovery SSH key is checked. Change the SSH key if required.
    2. Click Next.
    1. Review the summary and click Install cluster.

    After the installation process finishes, the cluster status is displayed on the Red Hat Assistant Installer portal, as shown in the following figure. You can monitor the installation progress from the portal.

    Figure 5.        Cluster installation status monitor

    1. Download the kubeconfig file and kubeadmin credentials from the portal. To verify the status of cluster nodes, run the following command:

    oc get nodes

    1. To verify the status of cluster operators, run the following command:

    oc get co

    Scaling up the cluster

    If you add compute nodes to scale up an OpenShift cluster that you installed using Assisted Installer, ensure that:

    • The compute node is powered off.
    • The DNS is updated with the A-record and CNAME entries of the compute node to be added.

    If the DNS is hosted on the CSAH node, update the /var/named/<zone> file, and then run the following command to restart the named service:

    systemctl restart named

    Expand an existing cluster

    To expand an existing cluster:

    1. Log in to the OpenShift Cluster Manager and select the cluster that is to be scaled up.
    1. Go to the Add Hosts tab and click Add hosts.

    Figure 6.        Add Hosts page on the Assisted Installer portal

    1. Follow the Add hosts wizard prompts to enter the host-related information.
      1. On the Cluster details tab, choose or enter the settings you want:

    i             Architecture and host network configuration: DHCP or Static
    Select Static Host Network Configuration and click Next.

    ii           In the Static Network Configurations tab, provide the DNS IP, machine network, and default gateway.

    1. If you need to create a bond, use the NMStateConfig sample file. Click Next.
    2. Provide the Host MAC address and IPv4 adress. Click Next.
    3. Paste in the SSH public key of the CSAH or admin node.
    1. Download the discovery ISO and boot the server.

    After a few minutes, the host is discovered and displayed on the Assisted Installer portal.

    1. If required, change the hostname of the nodes.
    2. Select the Role of the nodes: master or worker.
    3. To select the installation disk, expand the host details using the arrow to the left of the hostname, and then click Install ready hosts.

    The node status on the Assisted Installer portal changes to Installed and the node joins the cluster within a few minutes.

    1. To approve any pending CSR from the new node, run the following command:

    oc get csr -o name | xargs oc adm certificate approve

    1. To verify that the node is added to the cluster, run the following command:

    oc get nodes

The chapter also provides information about installing Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 on the CSAH node and running the cluster prerequisites.

Assisted Installer deployment

  • Expand an existing cluster

    To expand an existing cluster:

    1. Log in to the OpenShift Cluster Manager and select the cluster that is to be scaled up.
    1. Go to the Add Hosts tab and click Add hosts.

    Figure 6.        Add Hosts page on the Assisted Installer portal

    1. Follow the Add hosts wizard prompts to enter the host-related information.
      1. On the Cluster details tab, choose or enter the settings you want:

    i             Architecture and host network configuration: DHCP or Static
    Select Static Host Network Configuration and click Next.

    ii           In the Static Network Configurations tab, provide the DNS IP, machine network, and default gateway.

    1. If you need to create a bond, use the NMStateConfig sample file. Click Next.
    2. Provide the Host MAC address and IPv4 adress. Click Next.
    3. Paste in the SSH public key of the CSAH or admin node.
    1. Download the discovery ISO and boot the server.

    After a few minutes, the host is discovered and displayed on the Assisted Installer portal.

    1. If required, change the hostname of the nodes.
    2. Select the Role of the nodes: master or worker.
    3. To select the installation disk, expand the host details using the arrow to the left of the hostname, and then click Install ready hosts.

    The node status on the Assisted Installer portal changes to Installed and the node joins the cluster within a few minutes.

    1. To approve any pending CSR from the new node, run the following command:

    oc get csr -o name | xargs oc adm certificate approve

    1. To verify that the node is added to the cluster, run the following command:

    oc get nodes

Configuring OpenShift Container Platform authentication

  • Introduction

    OpenShift Container Platform supports different authentication methods based on the identity provider. For more information, see Understanding authentication. 

    This section describes how to configure users using the htpasswd identity provider.

    Create an admin user

    Note: Unless otherwise specified, run the following commands on the primary CSAH node as user core.

    To create an admin user:

    1. Create an htpasswd file on the CSAH node by running the following command:

    [core@csah ~]$ cd /home/core/openshift

    [core@csah openshift]$ htpasswd -c -B -b htpasswd ocpadmin Password1

    [core@csah openshift]$ htpasswd -b htpasswd ocpuser Password2

    1. Create a secret for passwd by running the following command:

    [core@csah openshift]$ oc create secret generic htpass-secret --from-file=htpasswd=/home/core/openshift/htpasswd -n openshift-config

    1. Create a CR and save the following contents to a file by running the following command:

    apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1

    kind: OAuth

    metadata:

      name: cluster

    spec:

      identityProviders:

      - name: htpasswd

        mappingMethod: claim

        type: HTPasswd

        htpasswd:

          fileData:

            name: htpass-secret

    1. Apply the CR by running the following command:

    [core@csah ~]$ oc apply -f <file name>

    1. To log in as the user that you created with htpasswd, run the following command:

    [core@csah ~]$ oc login -u <username>

    Authentication required for https://api.ipi414.dcws.lab:6443 (openshift)

    Username: <username>

    Password: <password>

    Login successful.

    You don’t have any projects. You can try to create a new project, by running oc new-project <projectname>

    Assign a cluster-admin role

    To assign a cluster-admin role to the admin user:

    1. Log in as kubeadmin and assign cluster-admin access by running the following command:

    [core@csah openshift]$ oc login -u kubeadmin -p xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx

    The following is sample output from the command:

    Login successful.

    You have access to 53 projects, the list has been suppressed. You can list all projects with ‘oc projects’
    Using project “default”.

    1. To ensure that the user is listed, run the following command:

    [core@csah ~]$ oc get users

    NAME       UID    FULL NAME   IDENTITIES

    ocpadmin   273ccf25-9b32-4b4d-aad4-503c5aa27eee               htpasswd:ocpadmin

    1. Get a list of all the available cluster roles by running the following command:

    [core@csah ~]$ oc get clusterrole --all-namespaces

    1. Assign the cluster-admin role to the user ocpadmin by running the following command:

    [core@csah ~]$ oc adm policy add-cluster-role-to-user cluster-admin ocpadmin

    clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/cluster-admin added:  “ocpadmin”

Configuring the Dell switches

  • Steps

    This section describes the Dell Networking OS10 initial out-of-band (OOB) management IP address configuration.

    Perform the following steps to set an IP address to the management network. Modify the sample configuration files as necessary, and then copy the modified switch file to the switches as running-config.

    1. Power on the switches, connect to the serial debug port, set the hostname, and configure a static IP address for the management 1/1/1 port. The following example uses an S5232F-1 switch:

    OS# configure terminal

    OS(config)# hostname S5232F-1

    S5232F-1(config)# interface mgmt 1/1/1

    S5232F-1(conf-if-ma-1/1/1)# no shutdown

    S5232F-1(conf-if-ma-1/1/1)# no ip address dhcp

    S5232F-1(conf-if-ma-1/1/1)# ip address 192.168.33.44/24

    S5232F-1(conf-if-ma-1/1/1)# exit

    S5232F-1(config)# management route 0.0.0.0/0 192.168.33.1

    1. Modify the sample switch configuration in <git clone dir>/examples as necessary (see Switch connectivity).
    2. Repeat the preceding steps for switch S5232F-2 and switch S3148, ensuring that the appropriate switch configuration file is copied and the IP addresses are correspondingly modified.

CSM for Resiliency

  • The CSM for Resiliency is part of the open-source suite of Kubernetes storage enablers for Dell products. This CSM is designed to make Kubernetes applications, including applications that use persistent storage, more resilient to various types of failure. The CSM can be enabled for PowerStore and PowerMax Storage arrays.

    Prerequisites

    The CSM for Resiliency acts solely on pods that have been assigned a designated label. This label must a key and a value that match what has been set in the resiliency module configuration. On startup, CSM for Resiliency generates a log message that displays the label key and value that are being used to monitor pods:

    labelSelector: {map[podmon.dellemc.com/driver:csi-powerstore]

    Install the CSM for Resiliency on PowerStore

    On the CSAH node:

    1. Complete steps 1 to 4 of Configure the PowerStore driver.
    1. Use this sample file to create the CSM for PowerStore by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Ensure that PowerStore pods are running:

    oc get pods -n powerstore

    NAME                                     READY   STATUS    RESTARTS      AGE  

    powerstore-controller-675c948954-j9b69   6/6     Running   0             83s  

    powerstore-controller-675c948954-wlkvv   6/6     Running   0             83s  

    powerstore-node-7f72v                    3/3     Running   0             83s  

    powerstore-node-c9bkn                    3/3     Running   0             83s  

    1. Use the sample file to create a StatefulSet by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Verify that the stateful set is created.

    Get the pods that have a podmon.dellemc.com/driver label by running the following command:

    oc get pods -l  podmon.dellemc.com/driver

    NAME                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE     IP             NODE                NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES

    sts-busybox-resiliency-0   1/1     Running   0          4m19s  

    1. Verify that the pod is created with the volume attached to it by running the following command:  

    [root@csah resiliency]# oc rsh sts-busybox-resiliency-0

    ~ $ df -h

Dell Container Storage Modules

  • Dell Container Storage Modules (CSMs) enable a simple and consistent integration and automation experience, extending enterprise storage capabilities. As part of this Dell design for an OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 deployment, the Dell OpenShift engineering team validated CSM Replication on PowerScale storage.

    Here is the support matrix for Dell CSM and CSI drivers:

    Table 3.      Dell CSM-CSI support matrix

    Container Storage Module

    CSI PowerFlex v2.9.1

    CSI PowerScale v2.9.1

Deploying OpenShift AI

  • Red Hat OpenShift AI is a platform for data scientists and developers of artificial intelligence (AI) applications. The platform provides a fully supported environment that lets you rapidly develop, train, test, and deploy machine learning models on-premises.

    Prerequisites

    Ensure that you have:

    • A running OpenShift Container Platform cluster, version 4.14, which is configured with a default storage class that can be dynamically provisioned.

    •        Cluster administrator privileges for your OpenShift Container Platform cluster.

    •        Completed registry deployment, as described in Provision the image registry storage.

Deploying OpenShift AI

  • Prerequisites

    Ensure that you have:

    • A running OpenShift Container Platform cluster, version 4.14, which is configured with a default storage class that can be dynamically provisioned.

    •        Cluster administrator privileges for your OpenShift Container Platform cluster.

    •        Completed registry deployment, as described in Provision the image registry storage.

    Steps

    To deploy OpenShift AI:

    1. Log in to the OpenShift platform web console as a cluster admin.
    1. Click Operators > OperatorHub.
    2. On the OperatorHub page, search for Red Hat OpenShift Data Science Operator, and then click the operator.

    Figure 32.    Installing Red Hat OpenShift Data Science Operator

    1. Click Install.
    2. Keep the default settings and click Install again.

      “Ready for Use” is displayed when the installation is complete.

    1. Click View Operator.
    2. To install OpenShift AI components, create a data science cluster object. To do this:
      1. Click Create DataScienceCluster.

    Figure 33.    Creating a DataScienceCluster

    1. Accept the default settings and click Create.

    Figure 34.    Creating a DataScienceCluster object

    The Status changes to Ready when the installation is complete.

    Figure 35.    DataScienceCluster custom resource

    Accessing the Red Hat OpenShift Data Science (RHODS) dashboard

    From the OpenShift Container Platform web console:

    1. Click the application launcher ().
    1. Click Red Hat OpenShift AI 

    You are redirected to the rhods-dashboard login page.

    1. Log in with your OpenShift credentials.

    The RHODS dashboard opens, as shown in the following figure:

    Figure 36.    RHODS dashboard

    1. To ensure that your data scientists can use compute-heavy workloads in their models, enable graphics processing units (GPUs) in OpenShift AI. For more information, see Installing the NVIDIA GPU Operator.

    Accelerator Profiles verification

    To view the reset migration-gpu-status instance, go to the the Instances tab on the AcceleratorProfile custom resource definition (CRD) details page.

    Figure 37.    Accelerator Profiles

    Creating a data science project

    Creating a project helps you organize your data science work in one place. You can enhance the capabilities of your project by creating workbenches and adding storage, data connections, and model servers to your project’s cluster.

    To create a data science project:

    1. Log in to the OpenShift AI dashboard and click Data Science Projects.
    2. Click Create data science project.
    1. Enter Name, resource name, and description values for your project and click Create.

    Figure 38.    Creating Data Science project

    A page opens where you can create workbenches, add cluster storage and data connections, import pipelines, and deploy models.

    Creating a sample project workbench

    1. Click Data Science Projects and select the name of the project.
    1. In the Workbenches section, click Create workbench.

    Figure 39.    Creating a data science project workbench

    1. Provide the following values:
    • Name: demo
    • Description: demo
    • Notebook image > Image Selection: Minimal Python
    • Version selection: 2023.2
    • Container Size: Small
    1. Configure the storage for your OpenShift AI cluster.
    2. Click Create Workbench.

    The status changes from “starting” to “running.”

    Figure 40.    Data Science project status

    1. Click Open to get started on the project.

    Figure 41.    Jupyter Notebook console

Deploying OpenShift Virtualization

  • Prerequisites

    Ensure that:

    • A default storage class is present on the cluster for dynamic allocation of persistent volumes.
    • An ISO is available for booting the VM.

    Steps

    To install OpenShift Virtualization:

    1. In the OpenShift Container Platform web console, select  Operators > OperatorHub.
    1. From the list of available operators, choose OpenShift Virtualization, and then click Install.

    Figure 27.    Installing the Open Virtualization operator

    1. Select Operators > Installed Operators and click OpenShift Virtualization.
    1. Click Create HyperConverged.

    Figure 28.    Creating a hyperconverged instance

    1. On the page that opens, keep or update the default values of the hyperconverged instance as required, and then click Create.

    When the deployment is complete, a Virtualization section is enabled in the OpenShift web console. Create a new virtual machine from the console, as described in the following section.

    Create a virtual machine

    To create a virtual machine:

    1. In the OpenShift Container Platform web console, select Virtualization and click Virtual Machines.
    1. Click Create VirtualMachine.

    A Create VirtualMachine from catalog page opens, as shown in the following figure:

    Figure 29.    Creating a virtual machine

    1. Select the template that you want and click CustomizeVirtualMachine.
    2. For templates where a boot source is unavailable, you can upload a boot ISO to the PVC to boot the VM and install the operating system, as shown in the following figure:

    Figure 30.    Customizing VM template parameters

    1. Check Boot from CD and select Upload local file as the CD source type.

    A PVC is created that uses the default storage class.

    1. Upload the ISO file and enter a Persistent Volume Claim value to specify the PVC size that is adequate for the uncompressed image and any additional space that is required.
    2. Select Blank to create a PVC using the default storage class as the disk source, and enter a value for the Disk size.
    3. Click Customize VirtualMachine parameters.

    The ISO starts uploading to the PVC.

    1. When the upload is complete, click Create VirtualMachine to create a virtual machine from the template.

    Figure 31.    Creating a virtual machine

    You can review and manage the virtual machines that you create from the web console.

    1. To manage a virtual machine, click Virtualization and select the required virtual machine to view or update the settings.

Document purpose

  • This guide provides:

    • A description of the infrastructure that is required to deploy and operate OpenShift Container Platform 4.14.
    • Validated steps for deploying a production-ready OpenShift Container Platform cluster on Dell PowerEdge servers and Dell PowerSwitch switches. This information facilitates readiness for Day-2 operations.
    • Links to sample configuration files in GitHub that show what values to specify in configuration processes.

    To ensure that your application operates smoothly, Dell Technologies recommends that you complete the validation steps in this guide before proceeding with development or production use.

    A companion design guide provides information about the architecture and design of the solution. The guide is available at the Dell Technologies Solutions Info Hub for Container Platforms.

    Typographical conventions

    Configuration instructions in this guide use certain conventions to identify commands and screen output.

    Command syntax is in Courier New font. Information that is specific to your environment is placed inside <> symbols and is in italics. For example:

    • Command reference: OS10(config)# hostname <hostname>
    • On the top S5232F-ON switch, enter: OS10(config)# hostname SW1

    This document may contain language from third-party content that is not under Dell's control and is not consistent with Dell's current guidelines for Dell's own content. When such third party content is updated by the relevant third parties, this guide will be revised accordingly.

Hosted Control Plane

  • Overview

    Control plane configurations for OpenShift clusters are deployable using either stand-alone or hosted control planes. The control plane in the standalone arrangement is hosted on specific physical or virtual machines. Building control planes as pods on a cluster using hosted control planes removes the requirement for separate virtual or physical computers for every control plane. For more information, see Hosted control planes overview.

Hosted Control Plane

  • Overview

    Control plane configurations for OpenShift clusters are deployable using either stand-alone or hosted control planes. The control plane in the standalone arrangement is hosted on specific physical or virtual machines. Building control planes as pods on a cluster using hosted control planes removes the requirement for separate virtual or physical computers for every control plane. For more information, see Hosted control planes overview.

    Prerequisites

    Ensure that:

    • An OpenShift cluster is installed using the IPI or Assisted Installer method.
    • CSI drivers are installed and a default StorageClass is configured on the cluster. 
    • Records are created for the API and ingress IP addresses of the hosted cluster.

    Point the API IP to the worker node of the hub cluster and the Ingress address to the worker node of the spoke cluster by running:

    api.<spoke cluster>.<hub cluster>.<domain> Worker node IP of Hub cluster

    api-int.<spoke cluster>.<hub cluster>.<domain> Worker node IP of Hub cluster

    *.apps.<spoke cluster>.<hub cluster>.<domain> Worker node IP of Spoke cluster

    Configure the hub cluster for HyperShift

    Perform the following steps:

    1. Install the Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes operator from the Operator hub.
    2. Log in to the OpenShift web console and select Operators > Operator Hub.
    3. Search for Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes and select it.

    Figure 15.     ACM operator Installation

    1. Click Install and install the operator under the default operator-provided namespace.
    2. Select Operators > Installed Operators and click Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes.
    3. Click Create MultiClusterHub CR.
    4. Verify that all pods are running:

    oc get pods -n open-cluster-management

    1. Verify that the MultiClusterEngine CR has the HyperShift component enabled by running the following command:

    oc get mce multiclusterengine -o yaml

    1. Verify that the HyperShift ManagedClusterAddOn is created in the local-cluster namespace by running the following command:

    oc get  managedclusteraddons.addon.open-cluster-management.io -n local-cluster

Hosted Control Plane

  • Enable the Central Infrastructure Management service

    To enable the service:

    1. Configure the provisioning resource to watch all namespaces:

    oc patch provisioning provisioning-configuration --type merge -p '{"spec":{"watchAllNamespaces": true }}'

    1. Use the sample file to create AgentServiceConfig by running the following command:

    oc create -f <file name>

    1. Enable the desired version in clusterimageset and modify the visible field to match the following output:

    oc edit clusterimageset img4.14.0-x86-64-appsub

    apiVersion: hive.openshift.io/v1

    kind: ClusterImageSet

    metadata:

      labels:

        channel: fast

        visible: "true"

      name: img4.14.0-x86-64-appsub

    1. Log in to the OpenShift web console and select All clusters from the dropdown menu.
    2. To build a new hosted control plane cluster on bare-metal servers, select Discover hosts to create host inventory.

    Figure 16.     ACM console

    1. Click Create Infrastructure environment to launch the wizard.

    Figure 17.    Infrastructure environment creation wizard

    1. Provide the following information:
      1. The name of the infrastructure environment.
      2. The network type: Static IP, bridges and bonds.
      3. The CPU architecture x86_64.
    2. Click Add credential for Infrastructure provider credentials and provide the following information:
    • A name for the credential secret and namespace.
    • The base DNS domain in the format <hub cluster>.<base domain>

    Click Next.

    1. Copy the pull secret and SSH key. Click Next.
    2. Review the details that you provided for the secret and click Add.
    3. After the credentials are added, click Create to launch the Infrastructure environment wizard, as shown in the following figure:

    Figure 18.    Infrastructure environment creation wizard

    1. After the infrastructure environment is created, click Add Hosts on the Hosts tab and select the Baseboard Management Controller (BMC).
    • Enter the Name, Hostname, and Boot NIC MAC Address of the bare-metal server.
    • Enter the BMC address in the following format:
    •  idrac-virtualmedia://<IDRAC IP of baremetal server>/redfish/v1/Systems/System.Embedded.1
    • Enter the login credentials of the iDRAC console.
    • Use the sample file to create the NMStateConfig to create a bond on nodes.
    • Provide a MAC address and NIC names for mapping.

    Click Create.

    Figure 19.              Adding Baseboard Management Controller hosts

    The bare-metal servers are booted using the RHCOS Live image. The status of the nodes that are displayed on the console changes from Registering -> Provisioning -> Provisioned -> Available.

    The following figure shows the available hosts:

    Figure 20.     Host inventory

    Create the hosted control plane

    To create the hosted control plane after the nodes are added:

    1. In the Clusters tab, select Host Inventory.

    Figure 21.     ACM console

    1. Select the Control plane type as Hosted.

    The Create Cluster wizard opens.

    1. In the Cluster details tab:
      1. Select the Infrastructure provider credentials from the dropdown menu.
      2. Enter the Cluster name, Base Domain, and OpenShift version, and paste in the Pull secret. Click Next.

    Figure 22.     Hosted control plane installation

    1. In the Node pools tab, select 3 as the number of hosts and click Next.
    2. In the Networking tab:
      1. Select NodePort as the API server publishing strategy.
      2. Enter a worker node IP address as the Host Address.
      3. Paste in the SSH key.

    Click Next.

    1. In the Review and Create tab, click Create.

    The cluster is installed. You can verify the host status from the Host Inventory tab, as shown in the following figure:

    Figure 23.     Hosted Control plane node status

    1. After the HyperShift cluster is installed, extract the kubeconfig and kubeadmin-passwords by running the following commands:

    oc -n <spoke cluster> extract secret/<spoke cluster>-admin-kubeconfig --to=- > <spoke cluster>-kubeconfig

    oc -n <spoke cluster> extract secret/<spoke cluster>-kubeadmin-password --to=- > <spoke cluster>-kubeadmin-password

    1. Run the following command from the CLI:

    oc get pods -n <spoke cluster namespace> --kubeconfig <path to the spoke cluster kubeconfig file>

    1. Scale out the ingress controller pods by running the following command:

    oc patch -n openshift-ingress-operator ingresscontroller/default --patch '{"spec":{"replicas": 3}}' --type=merge --kubeconfig=<path to spoke cluster kubeconfig file>

Introduction

  • Getting started

    Dell Technologies has provided sample switch configuration files to help you easily adapt and configure the switches that you use for the OpenShift Container Platform cluster.

    1. Clone the repository by running the following command:

    git clone https://github.com/dell-esg/openshift-bare-metal.git

    1. Check out the origin/ecws_ocp414 branch and go to the examples directory.

    Note: If you use different hardware or require different configurations, modify the configuration files correspondingly. The configurations that are described in this section are provided for guidance on how to set up the network.

    Port connections between switches

Introduction

  • Deployment options

    Use one of the following methods to deploy OpenShift Container Platform 4.14:

    • Full control: User provisioned infrastructure (UPI) deployment enables the user to provision, configure, and manage the required cluster infrastructure and resources: bootstrap machine, networking, load balancer, DNS, DHCP, and so on. For the deployment steps, see this GitHub file.
    • Automated: Installer-provisioned infrastructure (IPI) deployment uses the baseboard management controller (BMC) of each cluster host for provisioning. See and the following section of this guide.
    • IPI-based deployment.
    • Interactive: The Assisted Installer from the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console offers an interactive way to enter configurable parameters and generate a discovery ISO to boot the cluster nodes. See Assisted Installer for OpenShift Container Platform.
    • Local agent-based: This method uses the agent-based installer from the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console for clusters that are confined in an air-gapped network. You must download and configure the installer (access requires Red Hat login credentials). See Agent-based installer cluster deployment.

    For an overview of each of these methods, see Installing OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 and the following section of this guide.

IPI-based deployment

  • IPI deploys and configures the infrastructure on which an OpenShift Container Platform cluster runs. The CSAH node is used as the provisioner node for the deployment. The node runs the installation program and hosts the bootstrap VM that is required to deploy the OpenShift cluster.

    IPI deployment steps

    Perform the steps in Preparing the CSAH node. Then:

    1. Configure a network bridge on the CSAH node by running the following nmcli commands:

    # Create bridge interface

    nmcli connection add type bridge ifname baremetal con-name baremetal

    # Create bond interface with bridge baremetal as master

    nmcli connection add type bond con-name bond0 ifname bond0 bond.options "lacp_rate=1,miimon=100,mode=802.3ad,xmit_hash_policy=layer3+4" ipv4.method disabled ipv6.method ignore master baremetal

    # Add slaves to bond interfaces

    nmcli connection add type ethernet con-name bond-slave-0 ifname eno12399 master bond0 slave-type bond

    nmcli connection add type ethernet con-name bond-slave-1 ifname ens2f0 master bond0 slave-type bond

    # Set IP Address to baremetal interface

    nmcli connection modify baremetal ipv4.method manual ipv4.addresses 192.168.36.62/24 connection.autoconnect yes ipv4.gateway 192.168.36.1 ipv4.dns 192.168.36.51  ipv4.dns-search dcws.lab

    Note: Use "baremetal" as the bridge connection name and interface name.

    1. Download the pull secret from the Red Hat web console and save it in the /home/ansible/files/pullsecret file (access to the console requires Red Hat login credentials).
    2. Prepare and run the Ansible playbooks as user ansible.
    3. Update the YAML file containing information about the bootstrap, control-plane, and compute nodes.

    Note: Ensure that you modify only values in the file. Keys must always remain the same.

    1. To start the program, run the following command:

    [ansible@csah ~]$ cd <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/python

    [ansible@csah python]$ python3 generate_inventory_file.py

    –-run --id_user <idrac user> --id_pass <idrac password> –-nodes nodes_ipi.yaml

    Note: If the iDRAC user and password are the same across all the control-plane and compute nodes, run the program using the --id_user and --id_pass arguments.

    1. If there is a backup management node, enter yes at the following prompt. Otherwise, enter No.

    Is there a backup management node [yes/No]: No

    1. Select IPI as the install type and enter 2.

    installation type:

     1. UPI

     2. IPI

     3. Assisted Installer

    enter install type: 2

    1. In the task menu, select all the options in sequence and enter the required details.

     1: cluster install

     2: infra components

     3: review inventory file

     4: generate inventory file

     5: exit

    task choice for necessary inputs:

    supported cluster install options:

     1. Standard - 5+ node (3 control and 2+ compute)

     2. Compact - 3 node (converged control/compute nodes)

    enter cluster install option: 2

    option selected: 2

    Checking iDRAC connectivity for control nodes.

    etcd0 iDRAC is reachable. 

    etcd1 iDRAC is reachable. 

    etcd2 iDRAC is reachable. 

    press any key to continue

    The next set of questions relates to network bonding on the cluster nodes.

    1. If you select y to perform network bonding for control nodes, select interfaces for each node, as shown in the following example:

    Do you want to perform bonding for ‘control_nodes’ (y/No): y

    select network interfaces for node etcd0

    1 -> NIC.Integrated.1-1-1 [LinkUp]

    2 -> NIC.Integrated.1-2-1 [LinkDown]

    3 -> NIC.Slot.1-1-1 [LinkUp]

    4 -> NIC.Slot.1-2-1 [LinkDown]

    Select the interface used by etcd0 first bond interface: 1

    selected interface is: NIC.Integrated.1-1-1

    Select the interface used by etcd0 second bond interface: 3

    selected interface is: NIC.Slot.1-1-1

    For each question, a prompt is displayed for all the control-plane and compute nodes.

    1. Provide the disk name for the cluster nodes for the operating system installation. Do this for each cluster node.

    Note: Control planes have similar hardware, so the disk names are the same for all three control-plane nodes. A different disk name is selectable for each compute node.

    1. Enter a network type, machine CIDR, and API and Ingress IP addresses for the cluster.

    Note: A virtual API IP address provides an endpoint for all users to interact with and configure the platform. A virtual ingress IP address provides an endpoint for application traffic flowing from outside the cluster.

    1. To specify the location of the pull secret, run the following command:

    ensure disknames are available. Otherwise OpenShift install fails

    Enter the installation disk name (Example - /dev/sda or /dev/nvme0n1) for control plane nodes

    default [/dev/nvme0n1]:

    enter the network type (OVNKubernetes / OpenShiftSDN) : OVNKubernetes

    specify the network cidr of the external network (format x.x.x.x/x): 192.168.36.0/24

    adding machine_network_cidr: 192.168.36.0/24

    enter API virtual IP: 192.168.36.27

    adding api_ip: 192.168.36.27

    enter ingress virtual IP: 192.168.36.28

    adding wildcard_ip: 192.168.36.28

    enter pullsecret file location

    default [/home/ansible/files/pullsecret]:

    The task for infra components lets you configure a DNS server on the CSAH node or use an existing DNS in the network.

    1. Select the DNS, cluster, and zone options that you require. The following example deploys the DNS on the CSAH node:

    Do you want to install DNS on CSAH [yes/No]: yes

    specify a DNS forwarder if necessary (yes/No): yes

    enter the DNS forwarder IP: 10.8.8.8

    specify cluster name

    default [ocp]: ipi414

    specify zone file

    default [/var/named/ipi414.zones]:

    1. Review and generate the inventory file.

    The program creates two files in the <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/python directory: generated_inventory and ansible.yaml.

    1. Copy both files into the <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/ansible directory.
    2. As user ansible, run the playbooks by using the following command:

    [ansible@csah ansible] $ pwd

    /home/ansible/openshift-bare-metal/ansible

    [ansible@csah ansible] $ ansible-playbook -i generated_inventory ansible.yaml

    1. To trigger the cluster deployment, run the command that you generated in the /home/kni/cluster_install_command file:

    /usr/local/bin/openshift-baremetal-install --dir /home/kni/clusterconfigs --log-level debug create cluster

    1. Verify the installation status in the .openshift_install.log file by running the following command:

    tail -f /home/kni/clusterconfigs/.openshift_install.log

    1. Validate the status of the control-plane nodes by running the following command:

    oc get nodes

    The command produced the following sample output:

    oc get nodes 

    NAME             STATUS   ROLES                         AGE    VERSION

    etcd0.dcws.lab   Ready    control-plane,master,worker   3d9h   v1.27.8+4fab27b

    etcd1.dcws.lab   Ready    control-plane,master,worker   3d9h   v1.27.8+4fab27b

    etcd2.dcws.lab   Ready    control-plane,master,worker   3d9h   v1.27.8+4fab27b

    1. Run the oc get co command to view the cluster operator status.

    Scaling up the cluster

    You can scale up an existing OpenShift cluster by adding more compute nodes.

    Ensure that:

    • The compute node is powered off.
    • The DNS is updated with the A-record and CNAME entries of the compute node to be added.

    If DNS is hosted on the CSAH, update the /var/named/<zone> file and restart named service by running the following command:

    systemctl restart named

    Expand an existing cluster

    To expand an existing cluster:

    1. Use this sample yaml file and update the fields as needed. Run the following command:

     oc -n openshift-machine-api create -f <name of yaml file>

    The file creates two secrets. The first secret contains the NMState config, and the second contains the BMC credentials. These secrets are referenced in the BMC resource.

    The node is booted from the live CoreOS. The state progresses from Registering to Inspecting to Available.

    [root@csah ~]# oc get bmh -n openshift-machine-api

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get bmh -n openshift-machine-api

    NAME       STATE                    CONSUMER                ONLINE   ERROR   AGE

    compute0   available                                        true             14m

    etcd0      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-0   true             12h

    etcd1      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-1   true             12h

    etcd2      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-2   true             12h

    1. When the nodes are available, get the machine sets in the openshift-machine-api project and scale them up by running the following command:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get machinesets -n openshift-machine-api

    The following is sample output from the command:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get machinesets -n openshift-machine-api

    NAME                    DESIRED   CURRENT   READY   AVAILABLE   AGE

    ipi414-cj4ms-worker-0   0         0                             12h

    [root@csah ~]# oc scale machinesets ipi414-cj4ms-worker-0 -n openshift-machine-api --replicas 2

    1. Get the node state by running the following command:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get bmh -n openshift-machine-api

    The following is sample output from the command:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get bmh -n openshift-machine-api

    NAME       STATE                    CONSUMER                      ONLINE   ERROR   AGE

    compute0   provisioned              ipi414-cj4ms-worker-0-pdjv7   true             25m

    etcd0      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-0         true             17h

    etcd1      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-1         true             17h

    etcd2      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-2         true             17h

    The nodes progress from Available to Provisioning to Provisioned.

    1. After the nodes are provisioned, run the following command to approve the CSR:

    oc get csr -o name | xargs oc adm certificate approve

    1. Validate the state of the nodes and the cluster operators by running the following command:

    oc get nodes,co

    selected interface is: NIC.Slot.1-1-1

    For each question, a prompt is displayed for all the control-plane and compute nodes.

    1. Provide the disk name for the cluster nodes for the operating system installation. Do this for each cluster node.

    Note: Control planes have similar hardware, so the disk names are the same for all three control-plane nodes. A different disk name is selectable for each compute node.

    1. Enter a network type, machine CIDR, and API and Ingress IP addresses for the cluster.

    Note: A virtual API IP address provides an endpoint for all users to interact with and configure the platform. A virtual ingress IP address provides an endpoint for application traffic flowing from outside the cluster.

    1. To specify the location of the pull secret, run the following command:

    ensure disknames are available. Otherwise OpenShift install fails

    Enter the installation disk name (Example - /dev/sda or /dev/nvme0n1) for control plane nodes

    default [/dev/nvme0n1]:

    enter the network type (OVNKubernetes / OpenShiftSDN) : OVNKubernetes

    specify the network cidr of the external network (format x.x.x.x/x): 192.168.36.0/24

    adding machine_network_cidr: 192.168.36.0/24

    enter API virtual IP: 192.168.36.27

    adding api_ip: 192.168.36.27

    enter ingress virtual IP: 192.168.36.28

    adding wildcard_ip: 192.168.36.28

    enter pullsecret file location

    default [/home/ansible/files/pullsecret]:

    The task for infra components lets you configure a DNS server on the CSAH node or use an existing DNS in the network.

    1. Select the DNS, cluster, and zone options that you require. The following example deploys the DNS on the CSAH node:

    Do you want to install DNS on CSAH [yes/No]: yes

    specify a DNS forwarder if necessary (yes/No): yes

    enter the DNS forwarder IP: 10.8.8.8

    specify cluster name

    default [ocp]: ipi414

    specify zone file

    default [/var/named/ipi414.zones]:

    1. Review and generate the inventory file.

    The program creates two files in the <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/python directory: generated_inventory and ansible.yaml.

    1. Copy both files into the <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/ansible directory.
    2. As user ansible, run the playbooks by using the following command:

    [ansible@csah ansible] $ pwd

    /home/ansible/openshift-bare-metal/ansible

    [ansible@csah ansible] $ ansible-playbook -i generated_inventory ansible.yaml

    1. To trigger the cluster deployment, run the command that you generated in the /home/kni/cluster_install_command file:

    /usr/local/bin/openshift-baremetal-install --dir /home/kni/clusterconfigs --log-level debug create cluster

    1. Verify the installation status in the .openshift_install.log file by running the following command:

    tail -f /home/kni/clusterconfigs/.openshift_install.log

    1. Validate the status of the control-plane nodes by running the following command:

    oc get nodes

    The command produced the following sample output:

    oc get nodes 

    NAME             STATUS   ROLES                         AGE    VERSION

    etcd0.dcws.lab   Ready    control-plane,master,worker   3d9h   v1.27.8+4fab27b

    etcd1.dcws.lab   Ready    control-plane,master,worker   3d9h   v1.27.8+4fab27b

    etcd2.dcws.lab   Ready    control-plane,master,worker   3d9h   v1.27.8+4fab27b

    1. Run the oc get co command to view the cluster operator status.

IPI-based deployment

  • Scaling up the cluster

    You can scale up an existing OpenShift cluster by adding more compute nodes.

    Ensure that:

    • The compute node is powered off.
    • The DNS is updated with the A-record and CNAME entries of the compute node to be added.

    If DNS is hosted on the CSAH, update the /var/named/<zone> file and restart named service by running the following command:

    systemctl restart named

IPI-based deployment

  • Expand an existing cluster

    To expand an existing cluster:

    1. Use this sample yaml file and update the fields as needed. Run the following command:

     oc -n openshift-machine-api create -f <name of yaml file>

    The file creates two secrets. The first secret contains the NMState config, and the second contains the BMC credentials. These secrets are referenced in the BMC resource.

    The node is booted from the live CoreOS. The state progresses from Registering to Inspecting to Available.

    [root@csah ~]# oc get bmh -n openshift-machine-api

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get bmh -n openshift-machine-api

    NAME       STATE                    CONSUMER                ONLINE   ERROR   AGE

    compute0   available                                        true             14m

    etcd0      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-0   true             12h

    etcd1      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-1   true             12h

    etcd2      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-2   true             12h

    1. When the nodes are available, get the machine sets in the openshift-machine-api project and scale them up by running the following command:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get machinesets -n openshift-machine-api

    The following is sample output from the command:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get machinesets -n openshift-machine-api

    NAME                    DESIRED   CURRENT   READY   AVAILABLE   AGE

    ipi414-cj4ms-worker-0   0         0                             12h

    [root@csah ~]# oc scale machinesets ipi414-cj4ms-worker-0 -n openshift-machine-api --replicas 2

    1. Get the node state by running the following command:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get bmh -n openshift-machine-api

    The following is sample output from the command:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get bmh -n openshift-machine-api

    NAME       STATE                    CONSUMER                      ONLINE   ERROR   AGE

    compute0   provisioned              ipi414-cj4ms-worker-0-pdjv7   true             25m

    etcd0      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-0         true             17h

    etcd1      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-1         true             17h

    etcd2      externally provisioned   ipi414-cj4ms-master-2         true             17h

    The nodes progress from Available to Provisioning to Provisioned.

    1. After the nodes are provisioned, run the following command to approve the CSR:

    oc get csr -o name | xargs oc adm certificate approve

    1. Validate the state of the nodes and the cluster operators by running the following command:

    oc get nodes,co

IPI-based deployment with FIPS

  • This chapter describes the requirements for creating an OpenShift cluster with Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) enabled. The services that are required to create the cluster are set up in the CSAH node. The chapter also provides information about installing Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 on the CSAH node and running the cluster prerequisites.

    Preparing the CSAH node

    Note: To enable the cryptographic module self-checks that are mandated by FIPS 140, enable FIPS mode during the system installation.

    To install Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 on the CSAH node:

    1. Connect to the Integrated Dell Remote Access Controller (iDRAC) for installing Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
    1. Add the fips=1 option to the kernel command line during the system installation, as shown in the following figure:

    Figure 14.     RHEL 8.6 installation with FIPS enabled

    Note: Do not install any third-party software during the software selection stage.

    1. Click Begin Installation.

    After the installation, the system should start in FIPS mode automatically.

    1. Verify that FIPS mode is enabled by running the following command:

    [root@csah ~]$ fips-mode-setup --check

    FIPS mode is enabled.

    IPI deployment with FIPS Steps

    Perform the following tasks in the console as user root:

    1. To set the hostname, run the following command:

                  [root@localhost~]# hostnamectl set-hostname <hostname FQDN>

    1. Follow Step 1 in IPI deployment steps to create a bond and assign an IP to the CSAH node.
    2. To enable the ansible-2.9-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms repository, run the following commands:

    [root@csah ~]# subscription-manager register --username <subscription.user> --password <subscription.password> --force

    [root@csah ~]# subscription-manager attach --pool=<pool id>

    [root@csah ~]# subscription-manager repos --enable=ansible-2.9-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms

    1. To install the Red Hat Package Manager (RPMs), run the following command:

    [root@csah-amd ~]# yum install -y jq ansible python3-netaddr git

    1. Create a user to run the playbooks.

    Note: Do not use the username core. User core is part of the OpenShift cluster configuration and is a predefined user in CoreOS. In the (primary or secondary) CSAH node, user core is created using Ansible playbooks. The remainder of this guide assumes that user ansible runs the playbooks.

    [root@csah ~]# useradd ansible

    [root@csah ~]# passwd ansible

    Changing password for user ansible.

    New password:

    Retype new password:

    passwd: all authentication tokens updated successfully.

    1. As user root, provide sudoers permissions to user ansible by running the following command:

    [root@csah sudoers.d]# pwd

    /etc/sudoers.d

    [root@csah sudoers.d]# cat ansible

    ansible ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL

    1. As user ansible, set up password-less access to the CSAH FQDN by running the following command:

    [ansible@csah ~]$ ssh-keygen (press enter and go by defaults for the next set of questions)

    [ansible@csah ~]$ ssh-copy-id <FQDN>

    1. Download the Ansible playbooks from GitHub and check out branch ocp414_fips86 by running the following command:

    [ansible@csah ~]$ git clone https://github.com/dell-esg/openshift-bare-metal.git

    [ansible@csah ~]$ cd <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal

    [ansible@csah openshift-bare-metal]$ git checkout origin/ocp414_fips86

    1. Download the pull secret from the Red Hat Web console and save it as /home/ansible/files/pullsecret. 
    2. Prepare and run the Ansible playbooks as user ansible. 

    Update the YAML file that contains information about the bootstrap, control-plane, and compute nodes.  

    Note: Ensure that you only modify values in the YAML file. Keys must always remain the same. 

    1. Run the program. 

    Note: If the iDRAC user and password are the same across all control-plane and compute nodes, run the program with the --id_user and --id_pass arguments. 

    cd <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/python 

    [ansible@csah python]$ python3 generate_inventory_file.py –-run --id_user <idrac user> --id_pass <idrac password> –-nodes nodes_ipi.yaml 

    1. Follow steps 6-12 in IPI-based deployment to continue.
      In the infra components step, enter yes to enable FIPS:

    task choice for necessary inputs: 2

    Do you want to install DNS on CSAH [yes/No]: yes

    specify a DNS forwarder if necessary (yes/No): yes

    enter the DNS forwarder IP: 10.8.8.8

    specify cluster name

    default [ocp]: ipi-fips

    specify zone file

    default [/var/named/ipi-fips.zones]:

    adding zone_file: /var/named/ipi-fips.zones cluster: ipi-fips

    Do you want to install cluster with FIPS enabled [yes/No]: yes

    1. Review and generate the inventory file. 

    The program creates two files inside the <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/python directory: generated_inventory and ansible.yaml. Copy both the files into the <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal/ansible directory. 

    1. As user ansible, run the playbooks: 

    [ansible@csah-amd ansible] $ pwd 

    /home/ansible/openshift-bare-metal/ansible  

    [ansible@csah-amd ansible] $ ansible-playbook -i generated_inventory ansible.yaml 

    1. Start the cluster deployment by running the command you generated in the /home/kni/ cluster_install_command file: 

    /usr/local/bin/openshift-baremetal-install --dir /home/kni/clusterconfigs --log-level debug create cluster 

    1. Check the installation status in the  .openshift_install.log file:

    tail -f /home/kni/clusterconfigs/.openshift_install.log 

    1. Validate the status of the control-plane nodes by running the following command: 

    oc get nodes 

    NAME             STATUS   ROLES                         AGE    VERSION

    etcd0.dcws.lab   Ready    control-plane,master,worker   3d9h   v1.27.8+4fab27b

    etcd1.dcws.lab   Ready    control-plane,master,worker   3d9h   v1.27.8+4fab27b

    etcd2.dcws.lab   Ready    control-plane,master,worker   3d9h   v1.27.8+4fab27b

    1. Run oc get co to view the cluster operator status. 
    2. Use the following query to verify if the cluster-config-v1 ConfigMap contains the "FIPS" option:

    oc get cm cluster-config-v1 -n kube-system -o json | jq -r ‘.data’ | grep -I “fips”

    Alternatively, run the following command to confirm that FIPS mode is enabled:

    oc debug node/<nodename> -- chroot /host sh -c "fips-mode-setup --check"

NVIDIA GPU operator deployment

  • NVIDIA GPU drivers are required to provision GPU on OpenShift Container Shift Platform. These drivers enable Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) and allow workloads to consume GPU. The Dell OpenShift engineering team provisioned an NVIDIA H100 GPU on a compute node to validate the solution deployment.

    Install the NFD operator

    The Node Feature Discovery (NFD) operator is required for the NVIDIA GPU operator. To install the NFD operator:

    1. In the OpenShift Container Platform web console, select Operators > OperatorHub.
    2. Choose Node Feature Discovery from the list of available operators and click Install.

    Figure 43.    Installing the NFD operator

    1. On the Install Operator page, select a specific namespace on the cluster and click Install. The recommended namespace is openshift-nfd.
    2. Select Operators > Installed Operators. 
    3. Verify that Node Feature Discovery is listed in the openshift-nfd project with a status of Succeeded.
    4. Verify that the status of the nfd-controller-manager pod is “Running,” as shown in the following code snippet:

    [root@csah ~]# oc get pods -n openshift-nfd

    NAME                                     READY   STATUS    RESTARTS        AGE

    nfd-controller-manager-8c4b5d5cb-d76l4   2/2     Running   0               32s

    1. In the NodeFeatureDiscovery tab, create an NFD instance:
      1. Click Operators > Installed Operators and locate the Node Feature Discovery entry.
      2. Click NodeFeatureDiscovery under Provided APIs.
      3. Click Create NodeFeatureDiscovery.
      4. Click Create to start labeling the nodes in the cluster that have GPUs.

    The NFD operator uses vendor PCI IDs to identify hardware in a node. NVIDIA uses the PCI ID 10de.

    You can review the status of the NFD from the OpenShift Container Platform CLI.

    1. Verify that the new node labels have been added by running the following command:

    oc describe node <node name>

    Install the NVIDIA GPU

    Perform this task as the cluster administrator from the OpenShift Container Platform web console:

    1. Select Operators > OperatorHub  > All Projects.
    1. Search for NVIDIA GPU Operator and select it.

    Figure 44.    Installing the NVIDIA GPU operator

    1. Click Install.

    The suggested namespace is nvidia-gpu-operator.

    1. Review the status of the GPU operator pod by running the following command:

    oc get pods -n nvidia-gpu-operator

    A ClusterPolicy CRD is created. The ClusterPolicy configures the GPU stack, including the image, the repository, and pod restrictions and credentials.

    1. From the web console, click Operators > Installed Operators > NVIDIA GPU Operator.
    2. In the ClusterPolicy tab, click Create ClusterPolicy.

    The platform assigns the default name gpu-cluster-policy to the policy.

    1. Click Create.

    Figure 45.    Creating the ClusterPolicy

    The GPU operator installs the components that are required to set up the NVIDIA GPUs in the cluster.

    After 20 minutes, the status of the deployed gpu-cluster-policy for the NVIDIA GPU operator changes to State:ready.

    Figure 46.    Sample nvidia-smi command output

    Perform this task as the cluster administrator from the OpenShift Container Platform web console:

    Figure 44.    Installing the NVIDIA GPU operator

    1. Click Install.

    The suggested namespace is nvidia-gpu-operator.

    1. Review the status of the GPU operator pod by running the following command:

    oc get pods -n nvidia-gpu-operator

    A ClusterPolicy CRD is created. The ClusterPolicy configures the GPU stack, including the image, the repository, and pod restrictions and credentials.

    1. From the web console, click Operators > Installed Operators > NVIDIA GPU Operator.
    2. In the ClusterPolicy tab, click Create ClusterPolicy.

    The platform assigns the default name gpu-cluster-policy to the policy.

    1. Click Create.

    Figure 45.    Creating the ClusterPolicy

    The GPU operator installs the components that are required to set up the NVIDIA GPUs in the cluster.

    After 20 minutes, the status of the deployed gpu-cluster-policy for the NVIDIA GPU operator changes to State:ready.

    Figure 46.    Sample nvidia-smi command output

    NVIDIA GPU operator ClusterPolicy status

    To verify that GPU resources are available for pods, create a pod to run the nvidia-smi command. For the pod specification, see this sample file in GitHub.
