Preparing the CSAH node

  • Note: If needed, you can add a CSAH node to ensure redundancy.

    Start by installing Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.2 on the CSAH node. To do this:

    1. Connect to the Integrated Dell Remote Access Controller (iDRAC) for installing Red Hat Enterprise Linux by following the steps in the Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Installation Guide.
    1. Under Software Selection, ensure that Server with GUI is selected.

    The Ansible playbooks that are described in this guide use packages that are installed with the Server with GUI option.

    1. Click Begin Installation.
    2. After the installation is complete, perform the following tasks as user root:
      1. To set the hostname, run the following command:

                  [root@localhost~]# hostnamectl set-hostname <hostname FQDN>

    1. To register the CSAH node, run the following command:

    [root@csah ~]# subscription-manager register --username <subscription.user> --password <subscription.password> --force

    [root@csah ~]# subscription-manager attach --pool=<pool id>

    1. To install the Red Hat Package Manager (RPMs), run the following command as user root:

    [root@csah ~]# yum install ansible-core-2.14.9 python3-netaddr python3 jq git -y

    1. Create a user to run the playbooks by running the following commands.

    Note: Do not use the username core. User core is part of the OpenShift Container Platform cluster configuration and is a predefined user in CoreOS. In the (primary/secondary) CSAH node, user core is created using Ansible playbooks. The remainder of this guide assumes that user ansible runs the playbooks.

    [root@csah ~]# useradd ansible

    [root@csah ~]# passwd ansible

    Changing password for user ansible.

    New password:

    Retype new password:

    passwd: all authentication tokens updated successfully.

    1. As user root, provide sudoers permissions to user ansible by running the following command:

    [root@csah sudoers.d]# pwd

    /etc/sudoers.d

    [root@csah sudoers.d]# cat ansible

    ansible ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL

    1. As user ansible, set up password-less access to the CSAH FQDN by running the following command:

    [ansible@csah ~]$ ssh-keygen (press enter and go by defaults for the next set of questions)

    [ansible@csah ~]$ ssh-copy-id <FQDN>

    1. To install the ansible collection, run the following command as user ansible:

    [ansible@csah ~]$ ansible-galaxy collection install ansible.posix community.general ansible.utils

    1. Download the Ansible playbooks from GitHub and check out branch ecws_ocp414 by running the following command:

    [ansible@csah ~]$ git clone https://github.com/dell-esg/openshift-bare-metal.git

    [ansible@csah ~]$ cd <git clone dir>/openshift-bare-metal

    [ansible@csah openshift-bare-metal]$ git checkout origin/ecws_ocp414

    If there is a secondary CSAH node, continue with steps 9 through 11.

    1. To create a secondary CSAH node, repeat steps 1 through 7.

    Install Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 on the CSAH secondary node manually, and repeat steps 4 through 7 with the necessary modifications.

    1. As user root, add an entry for a secondary CSAH node in the primary CSAH node /etc/hosts file by running the following command:

    [root@csah ~]# cat /etc/hosts

    <IP Address of secondary csah> <hostname of secondary CSAH> <FQDN of secondary CSAH>

    Example:

    192.168.35.50 csah-sec csah-sec.dcws.lab

    1. As user ansible, set up passwordless access from the primary CSAH node to the secondary CSAH node by running the following command:

    [ansible@csah ~]$ ssh-copy-id <FQDN of secondary CSAH>

Provisioning PowerMax storage

  • The PowerMax storage system delivers high levels of performance and efficiency using an integrated machine learning (ML) engine. For more information, see Dell PowerMax NVMe Storage.

    Prerequisites

    Ensure that:

    • Storage pools have been created along with FC ports
    • iSCSI interfaces are configured

    Provision PowerMax storage

    To provision PowerMax storage:

    1. Use this sample file to create the namespace and secret by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    Note: Specify the secret name as powermax-creds and ensure that the username and password are base64 encoded.

    1. Use this sample file to create PowerMax Reverse Proxy. Update Unisphere fields as applicable by running the following command:

    oc create configmap powermax-reverseproxy-config --from-file <config yaml file> -n powermax

    1. Create a TLS secret that holds an SSL certificate and a private key, as required by the reverse proxy server. Run the following command:

    openssl genrsa -out tls.key 2048

    openssl req -new -x509 -sha256 -key tls.key -out tls.crt -days 3650

    oc create secret -n powermax tls revproxy-certs --cert=tls.crt --key=tls.key

    oc create secret -n powermax tls csirevproxy-tls-secret --cert=tls.crt --key=tls.key

    1. Create a YAML file for the PowerMax driver using the appropriate sample file:
    • For iSCI, use this sample file.
    • For FC, use this sample file.

    Update parameters such as the Unisphere IP address as necessary.

    1. Create the CR by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Ensure that the PowerMax pods are running in the powermax namespace by running the following command:

    oc get pods -n powermax

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    NAME                                        READY   STATUS             RESTARTS       AGE

    csipowermax-reverseproxy-6c6b8db57c-kbnml   1/1     Running            0              6m39s

    powermax-controller-6b8cd8444b-rrsbw        5/5     Running            0              6m38s

    powermax-controller-6b8cd8444b-wm9qs        5/5     Running            0              6m38s

    powermax-node-ftmjr                         2/2     Running            0              6m38s

    powermax-node-j556d                         2/2     Running            0              6m38s

    powermax-node-rj5sc                         2/2     Running            0              6m38s

    1. Use this sample file to create a YAML file for the storage class. Specify any additional parameters for the storage class as necessary.
    2. Create the storage class by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Verify that the FC storage class for PowerMax has been created by running the following command:

    oc get sc

    Create dynamic volumes

    To create dynamic FC volumes:

    1. Create a YAML file to create a PVC using this sample file.
    2. Create the dynamic PV by running the following command:

     oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Create a pod and mount the created pvc using this sample file.

     oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Verify that the volume pod is created with the volume attached to it by running the following command:

    oc get pvc

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    NAME                      STATUS   VOLUME            CAPACITY     ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   AGE

    dynamic-fc-powermax-pvc   Bound    pmax-1f708f78c4   10487040Ki   RWO            powermaxscfc   21s

    1. Verify that the volume is mounted on the pod by running the following command:

    oc rsh powermax-fc-pod

    The following code is sample output from the command:

    sh-4.4# df -h

    Filesystem          Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on

    overlay             1.5T   74G  1.4T   5% /

    tmpfs                64M     0   64M   0% /dev

    shm                  64M     0   64M   0% /dev/shm

    tmpfs               152G   94M  151G   1% /etc/hostname

    /dev/mapper/mpathc   10G   33M   10G   1% /mnt

    /dev/sda4           1.5T   74G  1.4T   5% /tmp

    tmpfs               755G   20K  755G   1% /run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount

    tmpfs               378G     0  378G   0% /proc/acpi

    tmpfs               378G     0  378G   0% /proc/scsi

    tmpfs               378G     0  378G   0% /sys/firmware

    Create PowerMax snapshots

    PowerMax CSI drivers support snapshots of volumes. Snapshots that you create can be used to create a volume and restore the data.

    1. Create a VolumeSnapshotClass based on this sample file:

                  oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Verify that the volume snapshot class is created by running the following command:

    NAME                  DRIVER                    DELETIONPOLICY   AGE

    powermax-snap-class   csi-powermax.dellemc.com   Delete           12s

    1. Create a snapshot based on this sample file:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Verify that the volume snapshots are created by running the following command:

    oc get volumesnapshot

    The following code is sample output from the command:

    NAME                READYTOUSE   SOURCEPVC                 SOURCESNAPSHOTCONTENT   RESTORESIZE   SNAPSHOTCLASS         SNAPSHOTCONTENT                                    CREATIONTIME   AGE

    powermax-snapshot   true         dynamic-fc-powermax-pvc      0             powermax-snap-class   snapcontent-59d02b49-0bc8-4db4-ab74-13b0ad29ee33   19s            20s

    1. Create a PVC for the snapshot based on this sample file. Run the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    The snapshot PVC contains the snapshot data from the source PVC.

Provisioning PowerScale storage

  • The PowerScale platform delivers high levels of performance and efficiency with an integrated ML engine. For more information, see Dell PowerScale Family.

    Prerequisites

    Ensure that:

    • The CSI operator is installed. See Install the Dell CSM operator.
    • Storage pools have been created along with the NFS setup as necessary.
    • Basic authentication is enabled on PowerScale. Run the following command:

    isi_gconfig -t web-config auth_basic=true

    Provision PowerScale Storage

    To provision PowerStore storage:

    1. Create a namespace by running the following command:

    oc new-project isilon

    1. Use this sample file to create a secret by running the following command:

    oc create secret generic isilon-creds -n isilon --from-file=config=<yaml file>

    1. Use this sample file to create an empty secret:

    oc create -f <empty_secret_file>

    1. Use this sample file to create a CSI PowerScale driver YAML file:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    Update the fields as required.

    1. Verify that the PowerScale pods are running:

    oc get pods -n isilon

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    NAME                                 READY   STATUS    RESTARTS       AGE

    isilon-controller-5557765dc8-9h9nt   6/6     Running   0              2m36s

    isilon-controller-5557765dc8-lbt99   6/6     Running   0              2m36s

    isilon-node-h2xvp                    2/2     Running   0              2m36s

    isilon-node-qz4kr                    2/2     Running   0              2m36s

    isilon-node-z98p7                    2/2     Running   0              2m36s

    1. Create a YAML file for the storage class based on this sample file.

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    Specify any additional parameters for the storage class as necessary.

    oc get sc

Provisioning PowerScale storage

  • Provision PowerScale Storage

    To provision PowerStore storage:

    1. Create a namespace by running the following command:

    oc new-project isilon

    1. Use this sample file to create a secret by running the following command:

    oc create secret generic isilon-creds -n isilon --from-file=config=<yaml file>

    1. Use this sample file to create an empty secret:

    oc create -f <empty_secret_file>

    1. Use this sample file to create a CSI PowerScale driver YAML file:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    Update the fields as required.

    1. Verify that the PowerScale pods are running:

    oc get pods -n isilon

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    NAME                                 READY   STATUS    RESTARTS       AGE

    isilon-controller-5557765dc8-9h9nt   6/6     Running   0              2m36s

    isilon-controller-5557765dc8-lbt99   6/6     Running   0              2m36s

    isilon-node-h2xvp                    2/2     Running   0              2m36s

    isilon-node-qz4kr                    2/2     Running   0              2m36s

    isilon-node-z98p7                    2/2     Running   0              2m36s

    1. Create a YAML file for the storage class based on this sample file.

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    Specify any additional parameters for the storage class as necessary.

    1. Verify that the storage class is created for using PowerScale storage by running the following command:

    oc get sc

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    NAME                                 PROVISIONER                  RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE      ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE

    isilon-sc                            csi-isilon.dellemc.com       Delete          Immediate              true                   12s

    Provision the image registry storage

    Before you perform application builds, configure the image registry for the cluster.

    To provision storage for the image registry, create a PVC and assign the storage to the image registry configuration.

    1. To create a PVC, create a YAML file based on this sample file.

    Note: Ensure that the namespace is openshift-image-registry. The recommended PV size is greater than 100 GB. Assign a volume that supports ReadWriteMany access mode.

    1. Use the YAML file that you created in step 1 to create the PVC by running the following command:

    [core@csah ~]$ oc create -f image.registry.yaml

    1. Edit the registry configuration to use the PVC by running the following command:

    [core@csah ~]$ oc edit configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io

    1. Update the following spec by running the following command:
      1. Change the value for managementState from the Removed default value to Managed.
      2. Add the PVC name as the storage key:

    spec:

      managementState: Managed

      storage:

        pvc:

          claim: isilon-nfs-image-registry

    Validate the image registry

    To validate the image registry:

    1. Verify that the AVAILABLE column displays True for all the cluster operators by running the following command:

    [core@csah ~]$ oc get co

    Note: During the verification of the image-registry cluster operator status, the status of cluster operators such as operator-lifecycle-manager and kube-apiserver might change. Check all the cluster operators before continuing.

    1. Ensure that the image registry pods are all in the Running state, as shown in the following command output:

    NAME                                               READY   STATUS      RESTARTS   AGE

    cluster-image-registry-operator-758d7d5dfb-4cx8z   1/1     Running     0          5d16h

    image-pruner-28419840-lfnw5                        0/1     Completed   0          2d4h

    image-pruner-28421280-r48x7                        0/1     Completed   0          28h 

    image-pruner-28422720-5mqqb                        0/1     Completed   0          4h21m

    image-registry-56c6798969-qh9qc                    1/1     Running     0          58s 

    node-ca-dfvgp                                      1/1     Running     1          5d19h

    node-ca-kscrc                                      1/1     Running     1          5d19h

    node-ca-nvp8z                                      1/1     Running     1          5d19h

    1. Verify that the registry storage ClaimName that is used for the image registry pod in the step 2 output matches the PVC name:

    [core@csah ~]$ oc describe pod image-registry-56c6798969-qh9qc -n openshift-image-registry | grep -i volumes -A 4

    Volumes:

      registry-storage:

       Type:       PersistentVolumeClaim (a reference to PersistentVolumeClaim in the same namespace)

        ClaimName:  isilon-nfs-image-registry

        ReadOnly:   false

    1. Connect to any control-plane or compute node in the cluster:

       [core@csah ~]$ oc debug nodes/etcd-0.dcws.lab

    Temporary namespace openshift-debug-w9cp7 is created for debugging node...

    Starting pod/etcd-0-debug-cc9qr ...

    To use host binaries, run `chroot /host`

    Pod IP: 192.168.36.64

    If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter.

    sh-4.4# chroot /host

    1. Log in as kubeadmin:

    sh-5.1# oc login -u kubeadmin -p RouYn-S6WUL-3MinU-RzH3h --server https://api.ipi414.dcws.lab:6443

    The server uses a certificate signed by an unknown authority.

    You can bypass the certificate check, but any data you send to the server could be intercepted by others.

    Use insecure connections? (y/n): y

    WARNING: Using insecure TLS client config. Setting this option is not supported!

    Login successful.

    You have access to 73 projects, the list has been suppressed. You can list all projects with 'oc projects'

    Using project "default".

    1. Test the connection to the image registry service that is listening in port 5000 by running the following command:

    sh-5.1# podman login -u kubeadmin -p $(oc whoami -t) image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000

    Login Succeeded!

Provisioning PowerStore storage

  • The PowerStore storage system delivers high levels of performance and efficiency with an integrated ML engine. For more information, see Dell PowerStore.

    Configure the PowerStore driver

    PowerStore supports FC, ISCSI, and NFS protocols using Dell CSI drivers. Setting the driver X-CSI_TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL to auto ensures that FC is used if FC ports are available in the compute node. Otherwise, iSCSI is used.

    Note: Modify the IP address and NAS server name appropriately.

    1. Create a configuration file with details about the PowerStore array based on this sample file.
    2. Use this sample file to create a secret file.
    3. Create a namespace by running the following command:

    oc create namespace powerstore

    1. Create a secret by running the following command:

    sed "s/CONFIG_YAML/`cat <config file name created in step 1> | base64 -w0`/g" <secret file name created in step 2> | oc apply -f -

    1. Create the driver file based on this sample file by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Ensure that the PowerStore pods are running in the powerstore namespace by running the following command:

    oc get pods -n powerstore

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    NAME                                    READY STATUS     RESTARTS   AGE

    powerstore-controller-78874bdf6f- 2z4z4  5/5 Running    0          39s

    powerstore-controller-78874bdf6f- bq56m  5/5 Running    0     39s

    powerstore-node-499p9                  2/2 Running    0     39s

    powerstore-node-br9zr                  2/2 Running    0     39s

    powerstore-node-gbcsz                  2/2 Running    0     39s

    1. Ensure that the CSM CR is created by running the following command:

    oc get csm/powerstore -n powerstore

    The following is sample output from the command:

    NAME         CREATIONTIME   CSIDRIVERTYPE   CONFIGVERSION   STATE

    powerstore   48s            powerstore      v2.9.0          Succeeded

    1. Create a YAML file for the storage class based on this sample file.

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    Specify any additional parameters for the storage class as needed.

    1. Verify that the storage class for PowerStore is created by running the following command:

    oc get sc

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    NAME                                 PROVISIONER                  RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE      ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE

    dellcsi-powerstore-sc-fc             csi-powerstore.dellemc.com   Delete          Immediate              false                  30s

    1. Using this sample file, create a YAML file for the NFS storage class by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    Specify additional parameters for the storage class as needed.

    1. Verify that the NFS storage class for PowerStore is created by running the following command:

    oc get sc

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    NAME                    PROVISIONER                  RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE   ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE

    powerstore-sc-nfs       csi-powerstore.dellemc.com   Delete          Immediate           false                  14s

    Create dynamic volumes

    1. Create a PVC based on this sample file by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Verify that the volume is created by running the following command:

    oc get pvc

    The following is sample output from the command:

    powerstore-pvc-fc   Bound    csivol-b609b63af9   10Gi       RWO            dellcsi-powerstore-sc-fc   2s

    1. Create a pod and mount a volume to the pod based on this sample file by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Verify that the pod is created, and the volume is attached to the pod by running the following command:

    oc rsh test-pod

    1. To check the mount points, run the df –h command at the prompt that appears.

    To create a PVC using iSCSI and NFS, use the corresponding sample files in GitHub.

    Create PowerStore snapshots

    PowerStore CSI drivers support snapshots of volumes. Create snapshots to back up the iSCSI, FC, or NFS volumes.

    1. Create the snapshot class VolumeSnapshotClass based on this sample file by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Verify that the volume snapshot class is created by running the following command:

    oc get volumesnapshotclass

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    NAME                    DRIVER                       DELETIONPOLICY   AGE

    powerstore-snap-class   csi-powerstore.dellemc.com   Delete           13s

    1. Use this sample file to create a snapshot by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Verify that the volume snapshots are created by running the following command:

    oc get volumesnapshot

    The following code is sample output from the command:

    NAME                  READYTOUSE   SOURCEPVC            SOURCESNAPSHOTCONTENT   RESTORESIZE   SNAPSHOTCLASS           SNAPSHOTCONTENT                                    CREATIONTIME   AGE

    powerstore-snapshot   true         powerstore-nfs-pvc                           3Gi           powerstore-snap-class   snapcontent-035eee19-458b-4f5a-b011-102d46491361   4s             9s

    1. Use this sample file to create a snapshot PVC by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    The snapshot PVC contains the snapshot data from the source PVC.

    oc get volumesnapshotclass

    The following code excerpt is sample output from the command:

    NAME                    DRIVER                       DELETIONPOLICY   AGE

    powerstore-snap-class   csi-powerstore.dellemc.com   Delete           13s

    1. Use this sample file to create a snapshot by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    1. Verify that the volume snapshots are created by running the following command:

    oc get volumesnapshot

    The following code is sample output from the command:

    NAME                  READYTOUSE   SOURCEPVC            SOURCESNAPSHOTCONTENT   RESTORESIZE   SNAPSHOTCLASS           SNAPSHOTCONTENT                                    CREATIONTIME   AGE

    powerstore-snapshot   true         powerstore-nfs-pvc                           3Gi           powerstore-snap-class   snapcontent-035eee19-458b-4f5a-b011-102d46491361   4s             9s

    1. Use this sample file to create a snapshot PVC by running the following command:

    oc create -f <yaml file>

    The snapshot PVC contains the snapshot data from the source PVC.

Solution introduction

  • Red Hat® OpenShift® Container Platform is an open-source application deployment platform based on Kubernetes container orchestration technology. Containers are stand-alone processes that run within their own environment and run-time context, independently of the underlying infrastructure. OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 helps you develop, deploy, and manage container-based applications.

    For more information, see the following documentation:

    • OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 Documentation
    • Product architecture

    The Dell Validated Design (DVD) for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 on Dell infrastructure provides tested, validated, and documented design guidance to help you rapidly deploy Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform on Dell infrastructure.

    Note: While you can rely on Red Hat Enterprise Linux security and container technologies to prevent intrusions and protect your data, some security vulnerabilities might persist. For information about security vulnerabilities in OpenShift Container Platform 4.14, see OpenShift Container Platform 4.14 Release Notes. For a general listing of Red Hat vulnerabilities, see Red Hat Product Security.

Switch connectivity

  • The following table shows the connections from each server to the switch ports with a 25 GbE NIC in PCI slot 2.

    • SW1 (S5232F-1) is connected to port 1 in PCI slot 2.
    • SW2 (S5232F-2) is connected to port 1 in PCI slot 3.
    • S3148 is connected to iDRAC.

    Table 2.      Server-to-switch port connections

    Role

    S5232F-2

    To modify the sample switch files for your environment:

    1. Download the switch configuration files from GitHub by running the following command:

                  git clone https://github.com/dell-esg/openshift-bare-metal.git

    1. Switch to the ecws_ocp414 branch by running the following command:

                  git checkout origin/ecws_ocp414

    Note: For all references to git directories in the following sections of this guide, ensure that you are using the ecws_ocp414 branch.

    1. Modify the sample switch configuration files in <git clone dir>/examples to match your VLAN and IP schemes.

    The deployment uses untagged VLANs that use switchport access for nodes and tagged port channels for switch uplinks.

Using a CSM operator to configure storage

  • Overview

    OpenShift Container Platform cluster administrators can map storage to containers. For a list of supported Persistent Volume (PV) plug-ins, see Types of PVs.

    Note: The Dell OpenShift engineering team validated the design for an OpenShift Container Platform deployment using Dell PowerMax, PowerScale, and PowerStore storage systems.

    This section addresses the following topics:

    • Prerequisites for installing CSI drivers
    • Multipath configuration across compute nodes
    • Installing the CSM operator
    • Installing CSI drivers for PowerMax, PowerScale, and PowerStore storage with support for FC, iSCSI, and NFS storage protocols
    • Creating dynamic PVs using CSI drivers

    Prerequisites

    Ensure that:

    • PowerMax, PowerScale, and PowerStore storage systems are configured (iSCSI, FC, NFS) and operational
    • FC switches are configured with required zones
    • Storage systems are accessible from compute nodes.

    Multipath configuration

    To configure multipath across compute nodes:

    1. Get the base64 contents of the multipath.conf file by running the following command:

    [core@csah multipathd]$ echo 'defaults {

    user_friendly_names yes

    find_multipaths yes

    }

    blacklist {

    }' | base64 -w0

    1. Use the sample link to create a MachineConfig YAML file and specify the base64 contents in the file. Run the following command:

    [core@csah multipathd]$ oc create -f <machine config YAML>

    Note: This machine configuration applies only to compute nodes. After the machine configuration file is created and applied, the compute nodes reboot one at a time.

    Install the Dell CSM operator

    The Dell CSM operator for OpenShift is available on the OpenShift embedded operator hub.

    Note: Install the CSM operator before you install any of the CSI drivers for the installed storage system.

    1. Log in to the OpenShift web console and select Operators > OperatorHub.
    2. Search for Dell CSM Operator, select the certified operator, and click Install.

    The Install Operator page opens, as shown in the following figure:

    Figure 26.    Installing the Dell CSM operator

    1. Select a namespace on the cluster and click Install.
    2. To validate the installation, run the following command:

    [core@csah ~]$ oc get pods -n openshift-operators

    The following code snippet shows sample output from the command:

    NAME                                                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE

    dell-csm-operator-controller-manager-5b6d4fd8f4-5pslz   1/1     Running   0          12d
